pointsOfSail.title: Points of Sail
pointsOfSail.learningGoal: Learning goal: recognise the main sailing angles to the wind, understand the no-go zone, and choose a basic sail trim for each course.

sections.title: What are points of sail?
paragraphs: A point of sail describes the angle between the boat’s heading and the direction the wind is coming from.
The same boat can feel completely different depending on this angle. Upwind sailing needs tighter sails. Downwind sailing needs eased sails.

sections.title: Start with the wind
paragraphs: Before naming the point of sail, first find the wind. Look at flags, ripples, tell-tales, other boats, smoke, waves and what you feel on your face.
In this prototype the wind is fixed from the top of the screen. Rotate the boat and watch how the point of sail changes.

sections.title: Basic trim idea
paragraphs: As the boat turns away from the wind, sails are usually eased out. As the boat turns toward the wind, sails are usually sheeted in.
This tool gives a simple first instruction. Real trimming also depends on boat type, wind strength, sea state, sail shape and the lesson goal.

keyTerms.definition: The area too close to the wind where the sails cannot drive the boat properly.
The boat is pointing too close to the wind and may stop or drift backward.
Sailing as close to the wind as practical, with sails trimmed in tight.
A course across the wind. Reaching is often comfortable and efficient.
Sailing downwind, with the wind mostly from behind.
Adjusting the sails in or out to match the course and wind angle.

commonMistakes: Looking only at the boat and forgetting to identify the wind direction first.
Pulling the sails in tight on every course, even when sailing across or away from the wind.
Trying to sail directly into the wind and wondering why the boat slows down.
Changing course without adjusting sail trim.
Thinking the labels matter more than the feel of the boat, the sail shape and the instructor’s safety instructions.
pointsOfSail.quickCheckIntro: Answer these quick questions to check the basic idea. Feedback appears instantly.

quickCheck.question: What should you identify before naming the point of sail?
quickCheck.feedbackCorrect: Correct. The point of sail is based on the boat’s angle to the wind.
quickCheck.feedbackIncorrect: Not quite. Start by identifying where the wind is coming from.

quickCheck.question: What usually happens to the sails as you bear away from upwind toward a reach?
options: They are pulled in tighter and tighter
They are removed from the mast
quickCheck.feedbackCorrect: Correct. As the boat turns away from the wind, the sails are usually eased.
quickCheck.feedbackIncorrect: Not quite. Turning away from the wind usually means easing the sails.

quickCheck.question: What happens in the no-go zone?
options: The sails may luff and the boat may lose drive
quickCheck.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Too close to the wind, the sails cannot drive efficiently.
quickCheck.feedbackIncorrect: Not quite. In the no-go zone the sails usually luff and drive is lost.
